description.narrative: Danida is providing core support to CDD to help the organisation implement the time slice of its five-year strategy that falls within the project period. The following five key areas of work are priority areas of action in the strategy – political and constitutional governance; economic and corporate governance; justice, peace and security; social exclusion and equity; and civil society environment. The support to CDD will fund the Corruption Watch project. Corruption Watch is of particular interest to the Embassy, since it is the only one of its type in Ghana and highly innovative. Corruption Watch is an innovative approach by Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) and Media to contribute to the fight against corruption by raising public awareness on corruption cases that have been opened, but have stalled in the process. Corruption Watch is a series of radio programmes essentially seeking to raise public awareness on corruption cases that have been opened, but have stalled in the process, thus highlighting the frequent reluctance of the relevant authorities to take corruption cases brought before them the whole way through investigation and prosecution to conviction. The objective is for the programmes to gradually generate public demand for ending the impunity that results from this practice. Persistence and thorough investigation are key principles of the initiative, and the cases brought up have generated numerous reactions from the involved authorities and injected new momentum in the cases presented.
